summary: A 1941 CCC-built 100-foot timber lookout in Wallowa County, now abandoned as a lookout, with a 2019 camera tower beside it.

facts.design: 100-foot open timber tower with a 7x7 observation cab and catwalk, plus a small residence cabin
facts.status_note: Still standing but no longer used as a lookout; a 2019 camera tower stands beside it.

staffing.status: No longer staffed as a lookout; firelookout.com says it was used for emergencies into the 1980s (page undated).

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps per NHLR; firelookout.com also gives 1941.
Forest Lookouts says the 100-foot tower and a one-room cabin were constructed in 1942.
A 2019 newspaper dates the wooden tower to 1946; this conflicts with the 1941 and 1942 accounts.
Mrs. Riley Chandler listed as lookout personnel.
Riley Chandler listed as lookout personnel.
A new foundation was built under the cabin.
Riley Chandler listed as lookout personnel.
Jim Lewis listed as lookout personnel.
Metal roofing installed on the lookout buildings.
Joan Sines listed as lookout personnel for 1968 to 1970.
Fire-detection camera system installed; a 2019 newspaper describes a 110-foot metal camera tower beside the wooden lookout.

corrections.why: Both NHLR and firelookout.com give the tower as 100 feet tall (about 30.5 m). 1.8 m does not match a 100-foot tower; the proposed value is the 100-foot figure converted to metres.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and firelookout.com give 1941. Forest Lookouts says the CCC project was under way in June 1941 and that the tower and cabin were constructed in 1942. The story uses 1941 as the build year and notes the 1942 construction of the tower and cabin.
NHLR gives a 7x7 cab and firelookout.com gives 6x6. Not resolved by the sources; the story reports both.
A 2019 newspaper gives 1946 for the wooden tower, which conflicts with the 1941 and 1942 accounts. Not resolved; the newspaper may be mistaken or may describe a different structure.

Forest Lookouts says the camera was installed on the lookout. The 2019 newspaper describes a separate 110-foot metal tower beside the wooden one. Probably the same site; the story follows the newspaper's description.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 1.8 is wrong (100-foot tower); see corrections. Build year (1941 vs 1942 finish vs 1946 in a 2019 newspaper) and cab size (7x7 vs 6x6) are unresolved. Firelookout.com is undated, so 'abandoned' is not dated. No source found on current public access, climbing or rental; access and visit keys omitted. Staffing names come from firelookout.com only. No new photo with a reusable licence was found.
